'''Peter E. Toschek''' (18 April 1933 – 25 June 2020<ref>{{cite web|title=Der FB Physik trauert um einen geschätzten Emeritus-Kollegen|periodical=|publisher=Universität Hamburg, Fachbereich Physik|url=https://www.physik.uni-hamburg.de/ueber-den-fachbereich/aktuelles/2020/20200626-nachruf-toschek.html|url-status=|access-date=|archive-url=|archive-date=|last=Maiwald|date=2020-06-26|language=de|pages=|quote=}}</ref>) was a German experimental physicist who researched [[nuclear physics]], [[quantum optics]], and [[laser physics]]. He is known as a pioneer of [[laser spectroscopy]] and for the first demonstration of single trapped atoms (ions). He was a professor at [[Hamburg University]].

==Biography==
Toschek studied physics in [[University of Göttingen|Göttingen]] and [[University of Bonn|Bonn]]. Supervised by [[Wolfgang Paul]], he defended his Ph.D. thesis in 1961. The topic of his dissertation was the scattering of Gallium atoms in defined Zeeman states by Argon and Helium. In 1963, he became a research assistant at the Institute for Applied Physics at [[Heidelberg University]]. There he founded the first German research group for laser spectroscopy which was soon joined by [[Theodor Hänsch]] (doctorate 1969). Toschek completed his habilitation in experimental physics in 1968. In 1972, he became a Professor at Heidelberg. In 1981, he accepted a chair in experimental physics at the [[University of Hamburg]]. There he and [[Günter Huber]] founded the Institute for Laser Physics in 1989. From 1980 to 1990, Toschek co-edited [[Optics Communications]]. Peter Toschek worked at [[Stanford University]] with [[Anthony E. Siegman|Tony Siegman]] (1972), at the [[Laboratoire Aimé-Cotton|Laboratoire Aimé Cotton]] in [[Orsay]], France, (1978/79), and as a Fellow of the [[JILA|Joint Institute for Laboratory Astrophysics (JILA)]] in [[Boulder, Colorado|Boulder]], Colorado (1986/87). He retired in 1998, but continued to be a scientifically active part of the Institute for Laser Physics.

==Research==
Since the 1960s, Peter Toschek and his associates developed new methods of [[laser spectroscopy]] like Doppler-free saturation spectroscopy <ref>{{cite journal |author1=Th. Hänsch |author2=P. Toschek | title = Measurement of neon atomic level parameters by laser differential spectrometry | journal = [[Physics Letters]] | volume = 20 | date = 1966-02-15| issue = 3| pages = 273–275| doi= 10.1016/0031-9163(66)90361-1|bibcode=1966PhL....20..273H }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |author1=Th. Hänsch |author2=P. Toschek | title = Laser differential spectrometry measurement on neon depolarization | journal = [[Physics Letters]] | volume = 22 | date = 1966-08-01| issue = 2| pages = 150–151| doi= 10.1016/0031-9163(66)90553-1|bibcode=1966PhL....22..150H }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |author1=Th. Hänsch |author2=P. Toschek | title = Observation of Saturation Peaks in a He-Ne Laser by Tuned Laser Differential Spectrometry | journal = IEEE Journal of Quantum Electronics | volume = 4 | date = 1968-07-01| issue = 7| pages = 467–468| doi= 10.1109/JQE.1968.1075367|bibcode=1968IJQE....4..467H }}</ref>  as well as the extremely sensitive intra-cavity absorption spectroscopy (ICAS).<ref>{{cite journal | author = T. Hansch | author2 = A.L. Schawlow | author2-link = Arthur Schawlow | author3 = P. Toschek | title = Ultrasensitive response of a CW dye laser to selective extinction | journal = IEEE Journal of Quantum Electronics | volume = 8 | date = 1972-10-01| issue = 10| pages = 802–804| doi= 10.1109/JQE.1972.1076854| bibcode = 1972IJQE....8..802H }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |author1=V. M. Baev |author2=T. Latz |author3=P. E. Toschek | title = Laser intracavity absorption spectroscopy | journal = Applied Physics B | volume = 69 | date = 1999-09-01| issue = 3| pages = 171–202| doi= 10.1007/s003400050793|bibcode=1999ApPhB..69..171B |s2cid=122403487 }}</ref> They observed non-linear interactions of light with atoms <ref>{{cite journal |author1=Th. Hänsch |author2=R. Keil |author3=A. Schabert |author4=Ch. Schmelzer |author5=P. Toschek | title = Interaction of Laser Light Waves by Dynamic Stark Splitting | journal = Zeitschrift für Physik | volume = 226 | date = 1969-06-01| issue = 3| pages = 293–296| doi= 10.1007/BF01392091|bibcode=1969ZPhy..226..293H |s2cid=123032224 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |author1=Th. Hänsch |author2=P.E. Toschek | title = Theory of a Three-Level Gas Laser Amplifier | journal = Zeitschrift für Physik | volume = 236 | date = 1970-06-01| issue = 3| pages = 213–244| doi= 10.1007/BF01394503|bibcode=1970ZPhy..236..213H |s2cid=121064455 }}</ref> like self-induced transparency of an absorber, and like the generation of singular optical oscillations (solitons).<ref>{{cite journal |author1=W. Krieger |author2=P. E. Toschek | title = Self-induced transparency on the 1.15-μm line of neon | journal = Physical Review A | volume = 11 | date = 1975-01-01| issue = 1| pages = 276–279| doi= 10.1103/PhysRevA.11.276|bibcode=1975PhRvA..11..276K }}</ref> In 1978, Toschek‘s research group was the first to demonstrate the cooling of atoms by laser light,<ref>{{cite journal |author1=W. Neuhauser |author2=M. Hohenstatt |author3=H. Dehmelt |author4=P. Toschek | title = Optical Sideband Cooling of Visible Atom Cloud Confined in Parabolic Well | journal = [[Physical Review Letters]] | volume = 41 | date = 1978-07-24| issue = 4| pages = 233–236| bibcode=1978PhRvL..41..233N|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.41.233}}</ref> just before [[David Wineland]] and co-workers. After Peter Toschek and [[Hans Georg Dehmelt]] having proposed, in 1975, a scheme for the realization and observation of single atomic ions,<ref>{{cite journal |author1=H. Dehmelt |author2=P. Toschek | title = Proposed visual detection laser spectroscopy on single Ba<sup>+</sup> ion | journal = Bulletin of the American Physical Society | volume = 20 | date = 1975-01-29| pages = 61}}</ref> [[Werner Neuhauser]], [[Martin Hohenstatt]] and Peter Toschek demonstrated in 1978, for the first time, the trapping and visual observation of a single atom, a Barium ion, which had been cooled by laser light down to a few mK above absolute zero temperature, and confined within a miniature quadrupole [[ion trap]].<ref>{{cite journal |author1=W. Neuhauser |author2=M. Hohenstatt |author3=P. E. Toschek |author4=H. Dehmelt | title = Localized visible Ba<sup>+</sup> mono-ion oscillator | journal = Physical Review A | volume = 22 | date = 1980-09-01| issue = 3| pages = 1137–1140| doi= 10.1103/PhysRevA.22.1137|bibcode=1980PhRvA..22.1137N }}</ref> This achievement made feasible the manipulation, quantum measurement and spectroscopy of individual atomic ions.<ref>[http://www.deutsches-museum.de/fileadmin/Content/040_BN/PDFs/Prismentexte/Das_sichtbare_Ion.pdf Deutsches Museum, Das sichtbare Ion]</ref> On such quantum objects Toschek and associates observed for the first time and reported in 1986 Niels Bohr's metaphorical "quantum jumps",<ref>{{cite journal |author1=Th. Sauter |author2=W. Neuhauser |author3=R. Blatt |author4=P. E. Toschek | title = Observation of Quantum Jumps | journal = [[Physical Review Letters]] | volume = 57 | date = 1986-10-06| issue = 14| pages = 1696–1698| bibcode=1986PhRvL..57.1696S|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.57.1696|pmid=10033521 }}</ref> simultaneously with and independent of similar observations by [[Hans Georg Dehmelt]] and co-workers. Other achievements include the first demonstration of a two-photon laser <ref>{{cite journal |author1=B. Nikolaus |author2=D. Z. Zhang |author3=P. E. Toschek | title = Two-Photon Laser | journal = [[Physical Review Letters]] | volume = 47 | date = 1981-07-20| issue = 3| pages = 171–173| bibcode=1981PhRvL..47..171N|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.47.171}}</ref> (1981), the quenching of quantum noise (in the difference frequency signal of two laser emission lines) by correlated spontaneous emission (1990),<ref>{{cite journal |author1=Michael P. Winters |author2=John L. Hall |author3=Peter E. Toschek | title = Correlated spontaneous emission in a Zeeman laser | journal = [[Physical Review Letters]] | volume = 65 | date = 1990-12-17| issue = 25| pages = 3116–3119| doi= 10.1103/PhysRevLett.65.3116 | pmid=10042785|bibcode=1990PhRvL..65.3116W }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |author1=Ingo Steiner |author2=Peter E. Toschek | title = Quenching Quantum Phase Noise: Correlated Spontaneous Emission versus Phase Locking | journal = [[Physical Review Letters]] | volume = 74 | date = 1995-06-05| issue = 23| pages = 4639–4642| doi= 10.1103/PhysRevLett.74.4639 | pmid=10058561|bibcode=1995PhRvL..74.4639S }}</ref> stochastic cooling of single ions (1995),<ref>{{cite journal |author1=J. Eschner |author2=B. Appasamy |author3=P. E. Toschek | title = Stochastic Cooling of a Trapped Ion by Null Detection of Its Fluorescence | journal = [[Physical Review Letters]] | volume = 74 | date = 1995-03-27| issue = 13| pages = 2435–2438| doi= 10.1103/PhysRevLett.74.2435 | pmid=10057927|bibcode=1995PhRvL..74.2435E }}</ref> the observation of the oscillation dynamics of trapped ions <ref>{{cite journal |author1=B. Appasamy |author2=Y. Stalgies |author3=P.E. Toschek | title = Measurement-Induced Vibrational Dynamics of a Trapped Ion | journal = [[Physical Review Letters]] | volume = 80 | date = 1998-03-30| issue = 13| pages = 2805–2808| bibcode=1998PhRvL..80.2805A|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.80.2805}}</ref> (1998), atomic interferometry on a single ion (1999) <ref>{{cite journal |author1=R. Huesmann |author2=Ch. Balzer |author3=Ph. Courteille |author4=W. Neuhauser |author5=P. E. Toschek | title = Single-Atom Interferometry | journal = [[Physical Review Letters]] | volume = 82 | date = 1999-02-22| issue = 8| pages = 1611–1615| bibcode=1999PhRvL..82.1611H|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.82.1611}}</ref> and unambiguous evidence of impeded evolution of an unstable quantum system by the system's observation, the Quantum Zeno effect (2000).<ref>{{cite journal |author1=Chr. Balzer |author2=R. Huesmann |author3=W. Neuhauser |author4=P. E. Toschek | title = The quantum Zeno effect – evolution of an atom impeded by measurement | journal = [[Optics Communications]] | volume = 180 | date = 2000-06-01| issue = 1–3| pages = 115–120| bibcode=2000OptCo.180..115B|arxiv=quant-ph/0105004|doi=10.1016/S0030-4018(00)00716-1|s2cid=33325666 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |author1=Gerhard Mack |author2=Sascha Wallentowitz |author3=Peter E. Toschek | title = Decoherence in generalized measurement and the quantum Zeno paradox | journal = Physics Reports | volume = 540 | date = 2014-07-01| issue = 1| pages = 1–23| doi= 10.1016/j.physrep.2014.02.004|bibcode=2014PhR...540....1M }}</ref>

Toschek’s former students or associates include [[Bernd Appasamy]], [[Valery Baev]], [[Rainer Blatt]], [[Klaus-Jochen Boller]], [[Philippe Courteille]], [[Jürgen Eschner]], [[Theodor Hänsch]], [[Werner Neuhauser]], [[Ingo Siemers]], [[Ingo Steiner]], and [[Zhang Dao-Zhong]].

==Awards==
In 1990 Peter Toschek received the Robert Wichard Pohl Prize of the [[German Physical Society]] (DPG). He has been a member of the [[Academy of Sciences and Humanities in Hamburg]] since 1994. In 2002, Toschek became a Fellow of the [[Optical Society of America]] (OSA). In 2015 he received the [[Herbert Walther Award]], jointly awarded by DPG and OSA.
